 -versus-
 State of Odisha .... Opp. Party
 Mr. P.C. Das, A.S.C.
 Coram:
 Justice A.K. Mohapatra
 Order
Order No. 20.07.2023
 02. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual  /Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State.
3. This is an application under Section 438, Cr.P.C. filed by the petitioners for anticipatory bail.

4. The petitioner is are seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with C.T. Case No.624 of 2022 arising out of Khantapada P.S. Case No.199 of 2022, pending in the court of learned J.M.F.C.(R), Balasore f o r c o m m i s s i o n o f o f f e n c e p u n i s h a b l e u n d e r S e c t i o n s 4 9 8 - A/294/323/307/326/354/376/511/506/406/379/34, I.P.C. and Section 4 of the D.P. Act.
5.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner, who happens to be the husband of the victim and there was some dissention between the husband and the wife.

Initially,
the petitioner filed an application for dissolution of marriage before the competent court and while the divorce proceeding is pending, the // 2 // victim wife has filed the present case to take revenge.
6. Considering the nature of allegation, gravity of offence and the facts of the case, I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

However, it is directed that in the event the petitioner surrenders and moves an application for bail before the learned court in seisin over the matter within a period of three weeks from today, he shall be released on bail on such terms and conditions as would be deemed just and proper by the court in seisin over the matter.
